result: The focused live Process-worker campaign passed: 1 passed in 5.25s. The complete live Prefect/PostgreSQL suite passed: 46 passed in 65.42s with no skips.
assertions: With the self-hosted Prefect API stopped, four bounded dispatcher ticks left all 32 accepted submissions accepted, without execution attempts, sink rows, or effect-ledger records.

Dispatcher status reported unusable prerequisites during the API outage. Redacted process-local diagnostics recorded four failed ticks and Prefect API failures without submission, flow-run, or payload identifiers.

After the Prefect API restarted against the same PostgreSQL database, 32 bounded one-item ticks dispatched the backlog. Each receipt named the expected accepted target and included a nonnegative queue age.

Separate Prefect Process-worker runs completed all 32 accepted targets. Each submission has one completed execution attempt, a successful canonical report, and one committed effect record; PostgreSQL contains the expected sink data.
The full live Prefect suite also passed, covering the other managed worker, dispatch, schedule, cancellation, deployment lifecycle, and recovery cases in this test group.

runtime.prefect_server: Separately supervised API process backed by a dedicated PostgreSQL database

fingerprints.source_sha256_method: SHA-256 over sorted repository-relative source paths and file bytes, with NUL separators.

limitations: The campaign covers a bounded 32-submission burst and four immediate failed ticks; it is not a sustained-capacity benchmark or a prolonged-outage test.
Only CPython 3.11.15, Prefect 3.7.8, PostgreSQL 16.13, and the Process pool were exercised locally.

This is workspace-source evidence, not a clean installed-wheel or remote CI run for the 32-submission change. Production identity-provider, third-party backend, broader simultaneous fault, and complete release qualification evidence remain open.

ci_configuration.database_service: Local PostgreSQL 16.13 service; test-specific schemas and Prefect database were cleaned after the test.
ci_configuration.server_process: Separately supervised Prefect API process with PostgreSQL persistence

cleanup: The test used unique tenant, workspace, submission, deployment, sink-table, effect-ledger, and Prefect database identities.
The test stopped its Prefect API process and dropped its dedicated Prefect database and sink/effect tables; the shared local PostgreSQL service was left running.
